## Introduction *[[3:37](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=217s)]* Acts chapter 17, because the enemy's new argument is that the other nations can be saved, built on 'there is no difference between the Jew and the Greek' and the gospel to the Gentiles. With Acts 17 and the history of the Greeks over the Israelites, this class arms you to deal with the discrepancies of Jew and Greek: the people Paul found in Thessalonica, Berea and Athens were Israelites, colonized and renamed by the Greeks. ## Scriptures Opened **[Acts 17:1-3](/bible/acts/17#v1)** *[[6:23](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=383s)]* > [1](/bible/acts/17#v1) Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews: > > [2](/bible/acts/17#v2) And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures, > > [3](/bible/acts/17#v3) Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ. - Look up the maps: every name in the scriptures shows our captivities, and as the names are called off you can see the Israelites were in all these regions of Greece. - Paul's manner was to go where the Jews were, and there was a synagogue of the Jews in every one of these cities. - He reasoned out of the scriptures that Christ must suffer and rise again, because the Jews did not believe on salvation in Jesus Christ; they still held to the law of animal sacrifice that Moses gave them. - He had to show them in the scriptures that the law of animal sacrifice was temporary; that is why Galatians says the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ. **[Acts 9:1-22](/bible/acts/9#v1)** *[[8:33](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=513s)]* > [1](/bible/acts/9#v1) And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest, > > [2](/bible/acts/9#v2) And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem. > > [3](/bible/acts/9#v3) And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven: > > [4](/bible/acts/9#v4) And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? > > [5](/bible/acts/9#v5) And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks. > > [6](/bible/acts/9#v6) And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do. > > [7](/bible/acts/9#v7) And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man. > > [8](/bible/acts/9#v8) And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus. > > [9](/bible/acts/9#v9) And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink. > > [10](/bible/acts/9#v10) And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord. > > [11](/bible/acts/9#v11) And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth, > > [12](/bible/acts/9#v12) And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight. > > [13](/bible/acts/9#v13) Then Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem: > > [14](/bible/acts/9#v14) And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on thy name. > > [15](/bible/acts/9#v15) But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: > > [16](/bible/acts/9#v16) For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake. > > [17](/bible/acts/9#v17) And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost. > > [18](/bible/acts/9#v18) And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized. > > [19](/bible/acts/9#v19) And when he had received meat, he was strengthened. Then was Saul certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus. > > [20](/bible/acts/9#v20) And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God. > > [21](/bible/acts/9#v21) But all that heard him were amazed, and said; Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests? > > [22](/bible/acts/9#v22) But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ. - Saul persecuted anyone who believed on salvation in Jesus Christ, and his persecution was so great the Messiah had to come back and tell him to stop. - Christ blinded him; Paul never met Christ when he walked the earth, and this was his first encounter with him. - He is a chosen vessel to bear Christ's name before the Gentiles, kings and the children of Israel; people read this and say salvation is open to the other nations. - The conflict in the New Testament was not whether to keep the law; it was whether to keep animal sacrifice for remission of sin or believe Christ died and his blood washes away our sins. - Saul increased in strength and confounded the Jews: that is why the bishop says read four chapters a day. We have to increase our strength in the scriptures to confound those that challenge us, not sit down and do debates. - The Jews took counsel to kill him because they could not prove him wrong; the same is done to us with slander, lies and videos. Precepts: - **[Isaiah 9:6](/bible/isaiah/9#v6)** > [6](/bible/isaiah/9#v6) For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace. Where the Old Testament shows Christ coming: the government on his shoulder, and his name the mighty God, the everlasting Father, the Prince of Peace. We will only get peace through Jesus Christ, not by aligning ourselves with the other nations. **[Acts 17:4-7](/bible/acts/17#v4)** *[[20:49](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=1249s)]* > [4](/bible/acts/17#v4) And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few. > > [5](/bible/acts/17#v5) But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people. > > [6](/bible/acts/17#v6) And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also; > > [7](/bible/acts/17#v7) Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus. - Some believed, and devout Greeks and chief women not a few; we will see why they were called Greeks. - The Jews which believed not were moved with envy: there is no place in the Bible where all twelve tribes got along, so do not be moved when people ask why the camps cannot get along. - They took lewd fellows of the baser sort: wicked lowlifes with no respect for marriage, women or community, who glorify violence and keep no Sabbath, following a man with his own plan. - They drew Jason and the brethren to the rulers of the city: some of these evil men work underhanded with the government. - 'These that have turned the world upside down' is what they say about us for teaching Christ is black and salvation is only for the twelve tribes; they attacked Paul's teaching not based on God but based on the government. - 'Another king, one Jesus' is what we profess, but we are not turning anybody against the government or attempting an insurrection. Precepts: - **[Matthew 10:5-7](/bible/matthew/10#v5)** > [5](/bible/matthew/10#v5) These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: > > [6](/bible/matthew/10#v6) But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. > > [7](/bible/matthew/10#v7) And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand. The great commission: go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel and preach the kingdom of heaven is at hand. A kingdom needs a king, and that king is Jesus Christ; America can keep its president. - **[Matthew 10:11-13](/bible/matthew/10#v11)** > [11](/bible/matthew/10#v11) And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go thence. > > [12](/bible/matthew/10#v12) And when ye come into an house, salute it. > > [13](/bible/matthew/10#v13) And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you. Inquire who is worthy: we are not forcing anyone to believe; if a house is not worthy, they will assault you. **[Acts 17:8-15](/bible/acts/17#v8)** *[[29:45](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=1785s)]* > [8](/bible/acts/17#v8) And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things. > > [9](/bible/acts/17#v9) And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go. > > [10](/bible/acts/17#v10) And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews. > > [11](/bible/acts/17#v11) These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. > > [12](/bible/acts/17#v12) Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few. > > [13](/bible/acts/17#v13) But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people. > > [14](/bible/acts/17#v14) And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still. > > [15](/bible/acts/17#v15) And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed. - Look at the proximity of Thessalonica and Berea on the map; Paul was moving through Greece and we have to familiarize ourselves with these names. - The Bereans were more noble: they received the word with all readiness of mind and were not argumentative, the same way some schools thrive because the spirits are more lively there. - They searched the scriptures daily whether those things were so; those who argue online come back with ChatGPT and Google, from the white man and not the scriptures. - Honorable women which were Greeks are like a woman today who says she is an American: they took the identity of the ones who colonized and enslaved them. - The Jews of Thessalonica followed Paul to Berea to stir up the people, the same way people follow us around: they know if this doctrine spreads it is over for them. **[Acts 17:16-17](/bible/acts/17#v16)** *[[36:52](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=2212s)]* > [16](/bible/acts/17#v16) Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry. > > [17](/bible/acts/17#v17) Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him. - Be ready to travel, as the bishop says; when Paul reached Athens he needed men with him to help him teach. - His spirit was stirred to see the city wholly given to idolatry, the same way we tell our people to let go of Christmas, Thanksgiving, birthdays and Mother's Day. - Everywhere he went there was a synagogue of the Jews; these were not Gentile nations as people suppose to you. - He disputed in the market daily; that is why we set up in front of supermarkets, laundromats and barber shops, where the traffic is, to show there is no white Jesus. **[Acts 17:18-21](/bible/acts/17#v18)** *[[38:28](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=2308s)]* > [18](/bible/acts/17#v18) Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection. > > [19](/bible/acts/17#v19) And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is? > > [20](/bible/acts/17#v20) For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean. > > [21](/bible/acts/17#v21) (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.) - The Epicureans were not a race of people but a belief system, named after the Greek philosopher Epicurus, no different from Egyptology or the FBA movement. - They called Paul a babbler and a setter forth of strange gods, the same way people look at us when we say God is a black man and only the twelve tribes will be saved. - The Athenians spent their time in nothing else but to hear some new thing, like those always on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube instead of following what the Most High said.
Reading from the Zondervan Bible dictionary, on the Epicureans and the Stoics *[[40:34](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=2434s)]* > Epicurean has two main meanings: a modern sense related to fine food and drink, and a historical sense rooted in ancient Greek philosophy. - So you had black people following the customs of the Greeks, just like in the colleges. You black people join Greek fraternities. You sisters join sororities and you speak about your sisters in these fraternities. Where did you get this from? The Greeks. Alpha, Delta, Gamma, whatever all that stupid stuff that y'all do. That's the Greek philosophy. And they brought it into the places of learning, into the colleges. And that's why you black people want to join it, 'cause it's stuff that white people, your white colonizers, put that philosophy, that thought into your mind. All your thoughts now are by your colonizers. They have nothing to do with God. So that's why we go into the scripture and we paint the picture to show that God's chosen people are the Israelites, and what you're doing is not right. > Modern culinary and luxury meaning. Definition: fond of or adapted to luxury, sensual indulgence and refined taste, especially regarding high-quality food and drink. - That's why a lot of those people, when they join those fraternities, they think they're better than everybody else. > Epicureanism: related to Epicurus, 341 to 270 BC, an ancient Greek philosopher, or his school of thought. - It was named after a man. His school of thought is where you get Epicureanism from. This was something that they were training the Jews to follow. > Stoic: a person who endures pain, hardship or difficulty without complaining, showing emotion or reacting with excess feeling. - I had the most stupidest argument, that they were trying to say that these Stoics are the other nations. A Stoic is a belief system, just like Epicurean is a belief system. - Meaning they just have a blank look on their face, a stoic look on their face. > It was founded in Athens around 300 BC by Zeno of Citium, who taught in a public colonnade called the Stoa Poikile. - This is 300 years before Christ. The Greeks had the Israelites in Greece following stoicism. - So the Epicureans and the Stoics was a belief system that Paul had to deal with, the same way today. Now we got FBAs attacking us. We got black people who believe in Islam attacking us. We got people who believe in Egyptology attacking us. And the list goes on. We got black politicians believing that we have to vote for a better life to fix things, when we're telling you no, you're not going to get things fixed by voting. You're going to get things fixed by the black Messiah. The people that you're listening to are liars. - So it's always been a problem, even before Christ, of our people following the ways of fake leaders, of ideologies, of theology, of different means of thought other than God.
**[Acts 17:22-27](/bible/acts/17#v22)** *[[48:29](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=2909s)]* > [22](/bible/acts/17#v22) Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. > > [23](/bible/acts/17#v23) For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. > > [24](/bible/acts/17#v24) God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; > > [25](/bible/acts/17#v25) Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things; > > [26](/bible/acts/17#v26) And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation; > > [27](/bible/acts/17#v27) That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us: - The altar to the unknown God: those people did not know God, only what the Greeks taught them, just as the Methodist, Baptist and Catholic do not know the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. - As Christ told the woman at the well, ye worship ye know not what; salvation is of the Jews. - God dwells not in temples made with hands, like the church people believe God is in. - He has determined the times and the bounds of their habitation: the Lord restricts our movement, and we have an appointed time before he comes to judge the earth. - Seek the Lord: return to God through believing on his son Jesus Christ; that is what Paul was teaching in Athens. **[2 Maccabees 6:1-6](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v1)** *[[51:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=3067s)]* > [1](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v1) Not long after this the king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers, and not to live after the laws of God: > > [2](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v2) And to pollute also the temple in Jerusalem, and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius; and that in Garizim, of Jupiter the Defender of strangers, as they did desire that dwelt in the place. > > [3](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v3) The coming in of this mischief was sore and grievous to the people: > > [4](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v4) For the temple was filled with riot and revelling by the Gentiles, who dallied with harlots, and had to do with women within the circuit of the holy places, and besides that brought in things that were not lawful. > > [5](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v5) The altar also was filled with profane things, which the law forbiddeth. > > [6](/bible/2-maccabees/6#v6) Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient fasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew. - This is where the problem in Athens started: the Greeks ruled for three hundred years before Christ, and Paul was dealing with that history. - The king sent an old man of Athens to compel the Jews to depart from the laws of their fathers; the government always wanted us to stop keeping the laws of God. - They polluted the temple and named it after Jupiter, and attacked it because we ruled as a theocracy: God say it and we obey it. - The temple filled with riot and revelling is the black church now, a party house; the focus on women was there from the time of the Greeks, which is why we have a dress code. - They forbade the Sabbath and the ancient feasts; that is why Christians go to church on Sunday, and why these things are new to us as we restore them. - Nor to profess himself to be a Jew: that is why they are mad when we say we are the real Jews. That is why they removed the book of Maccabees, so you could not put the pieces together.
Reading from *Manners of the Ancient Israelites* by Claude Fleury and Adam Clarke, Part III, Chapter III, "The State of the Jews under the Macedonians", pp. 170-171 *[[57:31](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=3451s)]* > Alexander the Great, being convinced of their affection and fidelity, gave them the province of Samaria, - So that's how we know there were Israelites in Samaria. I could prove it in the scripture, but I'm showing you that Alexander the Great, he was the first leader of the Greeks. > and exempted it from tribute; and when he built Alexandria, settled some Jews in it, granting them the same privileges as the other citizens, - Like America did. They'll give you some privileges, but when they get sick of you, they take them back. That's why you're losing your right to vote. You're losing any grants that they gave you for school. You're losing public housing. You're losing the lending practices to get a home. They're getting rid of that. They're going after Wells Fargo, and it's to target a specific people group. - Alexander gave them exempt from taxes and gave them a place. It's the same thing with us now. After they freed us from slavery and we fought for civil rights, they gave us certain liberties. Now you're seeing a whole campaign to take everything back. > till at last they also were called Macedonians. - So the Jews were calling themselves Macedonians. > Indeed, the first of the Ptolemies, - Ptolemy was one of Alexander's four generals. You had Ptolemy, Cassander, Seleucus and Lysimachus. > having taken Jerusalem by surprise, - He attacked Jerusalem by surprise. > carried great numbers of the Jews captives into Egypt, - And took the Israelites captive where? Into Egypt. So that's why when we read Isaiah chapter 11, it says that Jews have to be recovered from Egypt. Can we get that real quick?
**[Isaiah 11:11](/bible/isaiah/11#v11)** *[[59:40](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=3580s)]* > [11](/bible/isaiah/11#v11) And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea. - From Egypt. How did they get into Egypt? It told you in these writings that he took Jews captives into Egypt.
Reading from *Manners of the Ancient Israelites* by Claude Fleury and Adam Clarke, Part III, Chapter III, "The State of the Jews under the Macedonians", pp. 171-172 *[[1:00:07](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cyq9dzxYXaQ&t=3607s)]* > who were spread as far as Cyrene. - Cyrene is on that map. So it shows you from Egypt to Cyrene there were Israelites there. So we don't understand this displacement of these captivities, because they don't tell us that. They just tell us about the cargo slave ship from the transatlantic slave trade and the sub-Saharan slave trade with the Arabs. But prior to that, we know that Alexander and Ptolemy called Israelites Macedonians and, taking Jerusalem by surprise, carried great numbers of Jews captives into Egypt. So that's why it's prophesied in Isaiah there will be a remnant of Israel being recovered from Assyria and Egypt. > But afterwards finding how religious they were, - Oh, after he attacked us and saw how much we wanted to follow our religion, our beliefs. > and faithful to their oaths, - And we were faithful to keeping God's commandments. > he put some of them into his garrisons, and treated them so well, that it drew many more into that country. - So a lot of Israelites started coming, because they said, "Yo, these guys really believe in their God and their Bible." So a lot more Israelites started coming. > It is said that his son Philadelphus redeemed all the Jews that were slaves in his dominions, and sent great presents to Jerusalem to procure that translation which he got made of their law. - So the government was trying to butter us up. > They were also favoured by several kings of Syria. - The Syrian government was trying to butter us up. > Seleucus Nicanor gave them the right of citizens in the cities which he built in Asia Minor - That's why a lot of you are proud to call yourself Americans, 'cause certain liberties and amenities come with you identifying as an American. It started during the time of the Greeks. That's why it's called the Greco-Roman Empire. America is an extension of ancient Rome. America's doing the same thing now. > and Cœlo-Syria, and even in Antioch his capital, - Did not Paul go to Antioch? This was 300 years before Paul went to Antioch. > with privileges that they also enjoyed under the Romans. - Why? If they bow down to Roman rule, Rome gave them privileges. It's the same thing now. We're telling people that follow this same system, let go of our stuff and return back to God as Israelites. They don't want to hear that. > Antiochus the Great having received signal services from the Jews, granted considerable favours and immunities to the city of Jerusalem; - As long as the Israelites work with them, they will give them freedom, 'cause they don't believe in no god. All they care about is money and living the way they want. > and to secure Lydia and Phrygia, which were not quite sound in their allegiance, he established colonies of Jews there, giving them lands to cultivate and build on. - You pull that map up that I showed you. These are all the places that the Bible mentions. - Lydia and Phrygia, they had a little trouble there. Not quite sound in their allegiance to who? To the government. - So they always tried to find a way to get us to leave God. We'll give you land. We'll give you freedoms. We won't tax you. We'll give you loans. We'll let your kids go to school. The bottom line is they don't want you serving God as Israelites. > The first privilege that the Jews always asked upon these occasions was liberty to exercise their religion - Let us serve our God. We'll do what you want, but just let us serve our God. That was the first privilege that the Jews asked for. > and observe their law. - Let us keep the Sabbath. Let us follow the dietary law. Let us follow the dress code. That's what we were trying to work out with the government 300 years before Jesus Christ. > But as for the rest, they could not avoid learning many Grecian customs, - That's why Paul says there's no difference between the Jew and the Greek. - That's what Paul had to deal with. These were Jews learning Grecian customs. The government was trying to mold them to move away from serving God and follow Greek customs. > as they had Chaldean and others, - Because they were already following Babylonian customs. So the Greeks saw that and said, we need to bring them to our customs. - So every time the Israelites were in captivity: when a nation enslaves you, they change you and rename you. So that's why we were following Egyptian customs. We were following Chaldean customs. We were following Assyrian customs. Now the Greeks. This is historically documented. We got a little mixture of all our captivities inside of us. - They already were following Chaldean customs. They brought it over with them. > and particularly the Greek tongue, which was then become common throughout all the east, - That's why when you look up in the Zondervan Bible dictionary where it says Grecian or Greeks, it says Greek-speaking Jews, just like y'all now. Y'all speak Spanish, y'all speak English, you speak French, you speak Creole. Those are the tongues of your captives.
